rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a divine report that al-Fatiha is divided between God and servant: this middle declaration belongs to both, and the servant receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي شَطْرَيْنِ

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: Samura reports two Prophetic pauses, at prayer's start and after recitation of this ending; Imran objected but Ubayy confirmed Samura, and Qatada says the pause lets the reciter regain breath.
rows.anchor: عَنْ سَمُرَةَ بْنِ جُنْدُبٍ، قَالَ سَكْتَتَانِ حَفِظْتُهُمَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's prayer instructions: followers listen during the imam's recitation and say amin when he finishes with these words.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الإِمَامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ بِهِ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says people had stopped saying amin; the Prophet said it aloud after the Fatiha's closing words, loud enough for the first row to hear and the mosque to reverberate.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ تَرَكَ النَّاسُ التَّأْمِينَ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Imran b. Husayn recounts the Prophet rebuking a fighter who killed a man after he professed Islam: no one can inspect his heart; the man's body repeatedly rose from its grave.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ فَهَلاَّ شَقَقْتَ عَنْ بَطْنِهِ فَعَلِمْتَ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ ‏"‏

none: The camels and oath report is unrelated; its inshallah wording is incidental.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that during prostration the Prophet said this prayer of belief and surrender, ending with the verse's praise of God as the best of creators.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ كَانَ إِذَا سَجَدَ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ سَجَدْتُ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet's description of God's light and that God neither sleeps nor should sleep; Abu Ubayda then cites this verse after the report.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَنَامُ وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَنَامَ

none: The guidance and misguidance report does not discuss this verse; no verse wording is quoted.
The report concerns emancipation of a jointly owned slave and has no bearing on this verse.
The report praises Umar and does not discuss this verse; no verse wording is quoted.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet's teaching that remembrance of God is the best deed, most pleasing to God and highest in rank, better than wealth or combat.
rows.anchor: قَالُوا وَمَا ذَاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh b. Jabal says no deed saves a person more from God's punishment than remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل ما عمل امرؤ بعمل أنجى له من عذاب الله عز وجل من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Bedouin asks the Prophet for one Islamic practice to hold fast to; he replies that the man's tongue should remain moist with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ إِنَّ شَرَائِعَ الإِسْلَامِ قَدْ كَثُرَتْ عَلَىَّ

none: The hadith discusses the Prophet's pulpit and prayer; its question about what the pulpit was made from only coincides in wording.
